parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no traveller-facing criminalisation, no documented border or document friction, X-marker passports, freedom from gender-identity arrest affirmed 2011–2024, and working remedies (the 2015 compensation ruling; equal-treatment board). The dominant exposures are conditional rather than universal: birth-sex prison placement upheld by the supreme court in 2024, and recurring hate speech plus one 2024 murder of a migrant trans woman — a single case in a functioning rule-of-law state, background-tier rather than organised targeting. Anti-trans discourse during the age-limit debate is a climate signal. Strong institutional culture, high social tolerance, and no state threat-framing place this in the Low Risk band, modestly below the 0.95 anchors because custody placement and thin hate-crime coverage remain unresolved.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; no border or document-mismatch friction reported for trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Passports issued with male, female and X descriptors; self-ID since 2014; no gender-identity-based arrest grounds.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign-issued documents accepted without documented objection.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Supreme court (10 Sep 2024) held placing a trans inmate in a men's department is not a human-rights violation — birth-sex custody placement is lawful if a visitor is detained; 2013 asylum seeker was placed in a men's facility and sexually assaulted.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Rule of law, consular access norms, no gender-identity arrest grounds.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any police/immigration encounter that escalates to custody triggers the placement exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented for visitor-facing facilities; no bathroom or facility bans reported.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Equal-treatment framework covers gender identity and expression; housing and workplace protection documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Denial-of-access complaints reported by some trans people to the UN committee, remedy pathway via equal-treatment board.

care_services.exposure: Long waits (11–16 months HRT, 4–6 years surgery), stereotypical-presentation gatekeeping, restrictive youth pathway since 2023; mainly resident-facing.
care_services.protection: Gender incongruence declassified as mental illness; care system functions and discrimination law covers health settings.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing refills could encounter delays and gatekeeping, but denial is not traveller-targeted.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Anti-trans discourse intensified during the legal-recognition age debate; hate speech recurs annually; 38% of LGB respondents report differential treatment.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No state campaign targeting trans people; police not documented as perpetrators against visitors; no morality policing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Discourse is political debate, not state threat-framing of visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Youth care pathway requires extensive interviews, psychiatric evaluation and review of school/municipal records before hormone treatment; no surgery under 18 — relevant if a travelling minor sought care, not an entry or custody rule.
minors_guardians.protection: Hormone consent from age 15 without parental involvement; no criminal exposure for travelling families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family is not subject to investigation absent care-seeking.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Murder of a migrant trans woman in a hotel (Jul 2024); recurring hate speech; UN review noting threats against some trans people.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Functioning police and courts; discrimination case law awards compensation; single homicide, not a documented campaign; hate-crime statute does not name gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists but hate-crime coverage is narrower than the discrimination framework.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Hate-crime provision omits gender identity; prosecution counts and X-marker issuance unsourced; conversion-therapy ban pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Equal-treatment board, city-court precedent extending protection to gender identity, strong rule of law; barometer affirms freedom from arbitrary arrest yearly 2011–2024.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Silence on prosecutions is not evidence of failure in a well-documented state.

anchor_checks.comparison: Shares no-criminalisation, strong anti-discrimination machinery and respectful institutions, but 0.95-A documents prompt correction of even rural lapses and no custody-placement authority against trans people; this dossier documents a supreme-court ruling permitting birth-sex custody and a 2024 murder, so it sits below 0.95.

0.75-D features street attacks with partially unreliable police response; this jurisdiction has stronger institutional functioning, broader legal protection, and no documented policing problem, so it sits above 0.75.

Closely matched: both have robust equality law, working remedies, and residual uncertainty; the 0.85-A shelter-record hesitation and misdemeanour-level harassment resemble this dossier's hate-speech recurrence and custody-placement exposure, supporting ~0.85.
0.55-B documents routine secondary screening and discretionary refused entry; this dossier documents no such border friction at all, placing it far above 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters a regime with no gender-identity criminalisation, no documented border, document or facility restrictions, X-marker passports, and a years-long affirming record on arbitrary arrest. Protections are operative, not paper: courts extend equal-treatment law to gender identity and award compensation. The residual exposures are conditional: if detention occurs, the 2024 supreme-court ruling permits birth-sex prison placement, echoing the 2013 assault of a trans asylum seeker in a men's facility; and societal hate speech recurs annually with one lethal 2024 case against a migrant trans woman. Neither amounts to universal-exposure or organised targeting. Weighted together, this is a Low Risk jurisdiction at roughly 0.85, below the 0.95 anchors only for the custody ruling and unquantified hate-crime recourse.
